about.title: Turlock Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription:
Turlock is a working city. Between the shops along W Main Street and Geer Road, the businesses on N Golden State Boulevard, and the homes off Lander Avenue, people here rely on tools, appliances, vehicles, and equipment every day. When something does not perform as promised — a space heater that ignites, a tire that separates at highway speed, a child's car seat that fails on impact — the harm can be serious and the cause is not always obvious at first.

California treats these cases differently than an ordinary negligence claim. Under strict product liability, you generally do not have to prove the company was careless. You have to show the product had a defect in its design, its manufacturing, or its warnings, and that the defect caused your injury. Responsibility can reach the manufacturer, the distributor, and the retailer who sold it.

We are an attorney's office that handles product liability claims on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.title: You Don't Have to Prove Carelessness
items.desc: Because California applies strict liability to most product cases, we focus on the defect and the injury it caused, not on digging up proof that a company was negligent.

items.title: Every Link in the Chain Is on the Table
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and the Turlock retailer that sold the item can each be held responsible under California law, and our team can sort out who belongs in the claim.

items.title: Guidance on Preserving the Product
items.desc: The item that hurt you is the central piece of evidence. We advise you on keeping it, along with packaging, receipts, and photos, before anything is lost or discarded.

items.question: My car had a mechanical failure on Lander Avenue. Is that a product case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. Turlock recorded 331 injury collisions in 2025, and while most involve driver error, some trace back to a component that failed — brakes, tires, airbags, or steering. If a defect contributed to your crash, the manufacturer or parts supplier may be liable under strict liability in addition to any driver at fault. Keep the vehicle from being scrapped or repaired until our team has looked at it.

items.question: Do I still have a claim if I bought the product used or secondhand?
items.answer: Possibly. California's strict liability rules generally apply to products sold in the ordinary course of business, so the answer depends on who sold it and how. We can review the specific facts and tell you whether the manufacturer or an earlier seller in the chain may still be responsible.

items.question: What does it cost to work with us?
items.answer: Nothing. We handle product liability cases on contingency, meaning we are paid only if there is a recovery, and the terms are explained to you before you agree to anything.
